Requires a systemic feature (fever, sore throat or lymph nodes) in addition to clear discharge. The page's branch is selected by 'clear' vs 'pus'; 'fever, sore throat, enlarged lymph nodes' read as descriptive, so the rule is narrower than the page: a no-itch clear watery discharge alone never gets a diagnosis. rules.rule: Urgent: eye/vision symptoms with danger signs
rules.problem: Structure (and eye-finding (or ...)) and the Urgent level match the box heading. Two items over-fire or under-fire: unsited 'Chemical burn' makes any chemical burn anywhere Urgent for an eye-symptom patient, and only CVA (not TIA) is referenced, so a TIA diagnosis would not make the patient Urgent. Both BP criteria and the 1-week post-partum window are encoded correctly under the house conventions.

summary: The red box and all eight 'X likely' diagnoses are encoded with the right types, triggers and levels, and every concept exists in SNOMED. The most consequential problems are that 'stroke or TIA likely' only diagnoses (and escalates on) Cerebrovascular accident, dropping TIA, and that 'Chemical burn' carries no eye site, so under descendant matching any chemical burn makes an eye-symptom patient Urgent. Lesser points: 'whole eyelid' is dropped from orbital cellulitis (its discriminator against stye), the viral conjunctivitis rule is narrower than the page by requiring a systemic feature, and 'Localized enlarged lymph nodes' and the finding_site form of eyelid erythema have closer concepts.
